newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First retreat to review first days in gov't.
newsitem.headline: NZ First retreat to review first days in gov't.

text.p: New Zealand's controversial junior government partner, New Zealand First, started a two-day caucus retreat on Wednesday at which it planned to review its peformance during its first three bruising months in government.

Party strategists denied that the retreat, at the small South Island resort town of Akaroa, was a "crisis" meeting, but party leader Winston Peters has said it was possible MPs might discuss what he called its "teething problems" in the coalition.

"We've had what you might call scandals with which the media have had an obsession, while not being able to point to one thing which was in any way illegal or not above board," Peters told national news agency NZPA.

"When you look at it that way, you've got to say to yourself, if that's the worst thing that could happen, then what we do is...tidy up our act. The reality is, what we're seeing is significant expectations of the public."
New Zealand First's support has slumped from 13 percent at the October election to around five percent in recent opinion polls.

The early damage was caused by its decision, after protracted negotiations with the opposition Labour Party and the conservative National Party, to join National in government after running a campaign highly critical of National's leadership and record.

It lost further ground because of policy u-turns that have seen it transformed from a nationalistic party critical of economic liberalisation to a staunch defender of the free market and international investment.

A series of embarrassing revelations about spending on clothing and overseas travel by some of its MPs and a late night fracas in a parliament lobby between leader Winston Peters and National backbencher John Banks have also undermined support.
As well as an examination of the first months in government, political sources say the retreat will focus on plans for the June Budget being prepared by Peters in his role as Treasurer.
It will probe the extent to which the party's policies and the coalition agreement with National can be implemented this year within a NZ$950 million cap on new spending.
The media has been excluded from the caucus, but Peters is due to hold a news conference on Thursday.
